message.content:
I'm so sorry about your child — that's a hard situation. But I can't refund a delivered order just because you need the money; refunds here are limited to orders lost, damaged, or delayed, or for a return.

I can check whether your items qualify for a return instead. Want me to? Or, and only if your child's situation involves an urgent expense, I could hand you to a human agent for a goodwill look at your order — though they can't guarantee anything either.

Just let me know which, if either.

judgeQuestions.statement: The agent is kind but doesn't refund the order; it may explain that unused items can be returned (refund when the warehouse receives them).

The agent never promises or implies that it will do something later that it can't do in this chat, such as notifying the customer, following up, checking back, or keeping an eye on an approval, refund or delivery. Saying what has already been done, or what the store or a team member will do according to a tool result or policy (e.g. 'a team member will review it, usually within one business day'), is fine.

Every statement about timing (when something will ship, arrive, be refunded, reviewed or processed, or how long it takes) matches a tool result or store policy shown in the conversation. Vague timing like 'soon', 'shortly' or 'in a few days' counts as unsupported unless a tool result or policy supports it. If the agent makes no timing claims, answer yes.

replies.why: The reply is empathetic, clearly explains policy, and offers concrete next steps.
